original_value: In this article, we demonstrate the noise reduction and signal to noise ratio (SNR) enhancement in Brillouin optical time-domain analyzers (BOTDA). The results show that, although the main noise contribution comes from the Brillouin interaction itself, a simple low pass filtering on the detected radio frequency (RF) signal reduces remarkably the noise level of the BOTDA traces. The corresponding SNR enhancement depends on the employed cut-off frequency of the low pass filter. Due to the enhancement of the SNR, a mitigation of the standard deviation error of the Brillouin frequency shift (BFS) has been demonstrated. However, RF filters with low cut-off frequency could lead to distortions on the trace signals and therefore detection errors on a non-uniform BFS. The trade-off between the noise reduction and the signal distortion as well as an optimal cut-off frequency are discussed in detail.

result.paraphrase: This article demonstrates noise reduction and improved signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in Brillouin optical time-domain analyzers (BOTDA). The results indicate that, although the main noise contribution arises from the Brillouin interaction itself, simple low-pass filtering of the detected radio frequency (RF) signal markedly lowers the noise level of BOTDA traces. The degree of SNR improvement depends on the filter’s cut-off frequency. By improving SNR, the standard deviation error of the Brillouin frequency shift (BFS) is reduced. However, RF filters with low cut-off frequencies can distort trace signals and thus cause detection errors for non-uniform BFS. The trade-off between noise suppression and signal distortion, along with the optimal cut-off frequency, is discussed in detail.
